items.title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword proves the parry formula is far from stale, you just need to get freaky with it
items.summary: Parry fatigue? Not me.
items.body: Listen, I'll be the first to admit that I'm a little biased towards parry-based action games . Sekiro will forever be my favourite FromSoftware game because of just how excellently it captured the back-and-forth feeling of swordplay, not only with its timed deflection mechanic, but its mandate to have you keep the pressure on. But I appreciate that, for some, parry fatigue might be setting in. My fellow writer Mollie Taylor's sick of it , for instance—and I do understand. I think there are some games which use it as a bit of a crutch, and even the ones that don't can wear out their welcome. Take Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, for instance. I liked it, but I wouldn't want every turn-based RPG I play to have a timed block in it. Still, it's fun to have the occasional one where stats can be overcome with deft enough bumper hands. But to paint every parry-based system with the same brush seems short-sighted to me, because this deceptively simple mechanic has a ton of juice still left inside it: no other game proves this more than Onimusha: Way of the Sword, which, as far as I'm concerned, has broken new ground in terms of what parries can do. items.title: I never thought a fishing sim could be this fun, but How to Fish proves me wrong with its ridiculous physics, killer spider crabs, and classic co-op chaos
items.summary: I now know How to Fish, kinda.
items.body: I stand knee deep in a pool of blood. My coworkers, comrades, and friends reduced to food for soulless seagulls. Give a man a fish and he may throw it into the mouth of a weary fisherman, teach a man to fish and he shall bring forth the wrath of a spider crab who knows how to stab you with your own knife. This was my first experience of the new multiplayer fishing sim How to Fish , and now I can see why it's become such a smash-hit among bored and borderline-violent friendship groups. (Image credit: Dazed Games) It has a simple premise: you and up to four friends learn how to fish. The cycle of work involves players buying a basic fishing rod at first, using this to fish for, well, fish and crustaceans, and then beating them to death with your bare knuckles, brass knuckles, or a sick-ass knife. Then you can either eat your catch to replenish your health or hunger or feed it to the lonely fisherman who sits on the dock and gives you coins for your hard work. With the coins gained you can buy more tools to help you fish, like the knife, or supplies which you can use as bait, such as half a hotdog or an empty beer can. items.title: Blending Deus Ex with Escape from Butcher Bay, Deficit is one of the best-feeling indie immersive sims I've played—even if the stealth system needs serious work
items.summary: Playing the demo for Deficit was far from a net loss.
items.body: Immersive sims like Deus Ex and Dishonored are among the hardest kinds of games to make, so I always try to be supportive when an indie developer takes on the absurd challenge of creating one. Yet while there have been some good examples in recent years like Skin Deep and New Blood's early access Thief-like Gloomwood , a lot of the experiments in indie imsim design have been simply too janky for me to enjoy. Part of the problem is I'm a highly tactile player, and my primary concern when playing any game is whether it feels good beneath the fingers. If a game falls at that initial hurdle, then it's likely (though not inevitable) that I'll drop it pretty quickly. Fortunately, I had the opposite experience with Deficit , an indie imsim with such a strong sense of physicality that I kept playing the demo despite some clear issues. Developed by Item42, which previously created the cooperative shooter Perish , Deficit sees you play as a freelance spy in a dilapidated, dystopian world. You're tasked with infiltrating a sprawling fortress known as Hadrian's Wall to steal a device called the Interpolator, on behalf of a nameless client known as, well, The Client. items.summary: المدرب الإسباني يرفض المخاطرة
items.body: المدرب الإسباني يرفض المخاطرة كشف تشابي ألونسو مدرب تشيلسي، سبب غياب الثنائي ليفي كولويل ومويسيس كايسيدو، عن التشكيلة الأساسية للبلوز، أمام آرسنال على ملعب الإمارات، في الجولة الثالثة من الدوري الإنجليزي الممتاز. ونجح ألونسو في قيادة تشيلسي لتحقيق الفوز في أول جولتين أمام فولهام (3-2) وبرايتون (4-3)، بينما انتصر آرسنال على كوفينتري سيتي (3-0) وأستون فيلا (1-0). ويجلس كولويل على مقاعد البدلاء، بعدما شارك في أول مباراتين بشكل أساسي ، بينما يتواجد كايسيدو خارج القائمة. وقال ألونسو في تصريحاته لشبكة "سكاي سبورتس" قبل دقائق من انطلاق المباراة: "كولويل ليس ضمن التشكيلة الأساسية لأنه تعرض لانزعاجات بسيطة خلال الأسبوع". وعن غياب مويسيس كايسيدو أوضح وفقًا لما نقلته شبكة " بي بي سي " :  "كان قريبًا من المشاركة. لكن لا جدوى من المخاطرة في هذه اللحظة. علينا أن نكون حذرين". وبشأن صداقته مع ميكيل أرتيتا أتم ألونسو تصريحاته: "أتطلع لرؤيته. ولكن بمجرد أن يطلق الحكم صافرته، ستبدأ المباراة". يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة

items.summary: المسعفون هرعوا إلى أرض الملعب
items.body: المسعفون هرعوا إلى أرض الملعب  تعرض هاري ماجواير، لاعب مانشستر يونايتد، لإصابة مروعة في الوجه بعد ثوانٍ فقط من بداية مباراة فريقه وإيفرتون بالدوري الإنجليزي. حافظ المدافع البالغ من العمر 33 عامًا على مكانه في التشكيلة الأساسية بعد أن لعب دورًا رئيسيًا في فوز الشياطين الحمر 5-2 على إيبسويتش، الأسبوع الماضي. وتسبب ماجواير، الذي كان محور هدف جاكوب جريفز العكسي المثير للجدل في المباراة التي انتهت بالفوز، في بداية مؤلمة للقاء مع إيفرتون. يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات "كووورة" ووفقا لصحيفة " ذا صن "، لم يمضِ على بدء المباراة دقيقة واحدة حتى تورط اللاعب الإنجليزي في اصطدام مروع بالرأس مع مهاجم فريق إيفرتون، ثيرنو باري. وهرع المسعفون إلى أرض الملعب بعد أن سقط ماجواير أرضاً إثر الاصطدام المقلق. بدأ الدم يتدفق من أنف قلب الدفاع فور وصوله إلى ملعب هيل ديكنسون. كما شوهد زملاء الفريق وهم يتجمعون حول ماجواير خوفاً من أن يضطر المدرب مايكل كاريك إلى إجراء تبديل مبكر. لكن الطاقم الطبي لمانشستر يونايتد تمكن من سد أنف ماجواير لوقف تدفق الدم المستمر. وعلى الرغم من خسارته في التحدي الجوي مع باري، إلا أنه تمكن من الاستمرار. يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات "كووورة"

items.body: خلال مواجهة المستايا تلقى برشلونة، ضربة قوية خلال مواجهة فالنسيا على ملعب ميستايا، رغم تقدمه بهدفين دون رد عن طريق لامين يامال وفيرمين لوبيز، بعدما اضطر إريك جارسيا إلى مغادرة الملعب قبل مرور نصف ساعة، إثر تعرضه لضربة قوية غير مقصودة على مستوى الأنف. وتعرض جارسيا للإصابة بعد احتكاك مع رودري، ولم يتمكن قلب دفاع برشلونة من مواصلة المباراة، ليقرر الجهاز الفني استبداله بجولز كوندي عقب فترة استراحة شرب الماء، في انتكاسة للفريق خلال مواجهة فرض سيطرته على مجرياتها منذ البداية. وأظهرت الصور الأولية أن الإصابة لا تبدو خطيرة، إلا أن المدافع الإسباني قد يكون تعرض لانحراف في الحاجز الأنفي، بينما غادر أرض الملعب سيرًا على قدميه برفقة الطبيب برونا، الذي شرح طبيعة الإصابة لبقية لاعبي برشلونة. وتعيد الإصابة إلى الأذهان معاناة جارسيا السابقة مع إصابات الأنف، بعدما تعرض لكسر خلال الموسم الماضي واضطر إلى خوض عدة مباريات مرتديًا قناعًا لحماية أنفه. كان مدافع برشلونة قد أصيب خلال مواجهة كلوب بروج في دوري أبطال أوروبا مطلع نوفمبر من الموسم الماضي، وارتدى قناعًا واقيًا لعدة أسابيع، قبل أن يتعافى ويعود إلى اللعب بصورة طبيعية.

items.summary: Rat's entertainment.
items.body: I was largely nonplussed by Gamescom's Opening Night Live , particularly its relentless barrage of identikit fantasy action games that I struggled to tell apart. But one game stood out like a rat-powered computer in an elven glade, and that was Ontos , Frictional Games' latest horror adventure/existential crisis generator. The Gamescom trailer was a barrage of unsettling, distinctive imagery, from rodent server-racks to slack-jawed dudes with electrodes protruding from their heads. I was instantly intrigued and keen to learn more, so I was delighted to discover that Frictional graced us with a longer look at Ontos in action. The 10-minute showcase focuses on the same part of the game as the shorter trailer. But it adds significant context to how Ontos plays and the kinds of challenges you'll be dealing with. It starts with the player character—a woman named Aditi—arriving at the hospital wing of Ontos' repurposed 'Moon Hotel' Samsara via an internal railway system, before exploring the wing and unpicking an experiment run by a scientist called Crombie. items.body: Despite more than a year of updates and at least one massive overhaul, Civilization 7 remains as stubbornly divisive as ever. May's enormous Test of Time update brought significant mechanical reworks and a fresh influx of players to Firaxis' latest entry in the 4X series. But with Steam reviews still sitting at ' Mixed' , with 51% positive, it ultimately did little to shift player opinion. This is partly because numerous aspects of Civ 7 are still rudimentary compared to previous games, including the ability to wage nuclear war While Firaxis' latest allows players to drop atom bombs on their enemies via World War 2 bombers, its final, modern age ends in 1950, meaning many advanced technologies including nuclear submarines and ICBMs are not featured in the game. Fortunately, this is going to change. Alongside the release of update 1.5.0 —which adds features like improved resource generation and an Earth map where your faction starts at their historically-accurate location—Firaxis outlined its plans for the sequel over the next 12 months. items.body: Given that Anthem and Mass Effect Andromeda were widely considered disappointments, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard had a divisive reception, there's a certain amount of skepticism about the Mass Effect game BioWare is currently working on. Some have even suggested it might not come out at all . Armando Troisi, a cinematic designer on the Mass Effect trilogy and lead cinematic designer on Mass Effect 2, thinks it's all a bit much. "I think BioWare, when they break it down and do that singleplayer, interactive narrative-driven, deep combat, progression-driven game, really, there's nobody that can touch them," Troisi told FRVR . "It's kind of like the [Master] Chief, it's like going on a walkabout and finding themselves and coming back. I think BioWare can do it if we just leave them alone to do what they do best." Troisi said that when he was working at BioWare the studio knew what kind of game it was best at making, and that all they need is to get back to that. "The vision was always clear," he said. It's tough enough to stand out in the games market these days, let alone as a 2D platformer, so I'm always excited when one really breaks through and catches my eye. items.title: This free lockpicking puzzler you can play in your browser is unexpectedly one of the most thrilling games I've encountered this year
items.summary: Lockpicks-11 is a fiendish delight.
items.body: I love lockpicking minigames, especially when representatively they're as far away from the act of lockpicking as possible. While I admire the elegance of Bethesda's bobby-pin/screwdriver system seen in Fallout 4 , I'm much more interested in the weirder solutions like Splinter Cell 's baffling pin-flicking system, or Gothic Remake 's absurdly elaborate sliding puzzle system. I love how developers have tried so many ways to represent the act of lockpicking, and that despite this nobody has 'solved' the problem of virtual lockpicking yet (though Bethesda has arguably come closest). Inevitably, then, I was drawn to the idea of a game that is all about lockpicking. But I never expected that it could be as imaginative and thrilling as Lockpicks-11 . An entry for Ludum Dare 57, Lockpicks-11 places you in the role of an unnamed thief in the middle of a heist. Yet rather than being a fully fledged burglary simulator like Thief, Lockpicks-11 distils the act of larceny to a linear sequence of locked doors. items.title: Me: You can now run DLSS 5 on AMD GPUs. My RX 9070 XT: Please stop, it hurts us
items.summary: A new app allows you to inject DLSS Neural Rendering deep into games even if you're running an AMD card. You probably won't want to, though.
items.body: Another day, another DLSS 5 story that actually kinda doesn't involve Nvidia itself doing anything, because it seems now AMD GPU owners can get in on the act. A new homebrew app has been released on Github that will allow you to run the DLSS Neural Rendering feature on a Radeon GPU. I've tried it and it works, but damn does it hurt the poor Radeon silicon. From having DLSS 5 .dll files plucked from an early access version of NBA 2K27, we've had modders working hard to create surprisingly polished ways to essentially get the tech working in practically any game , even if it doesn't natively support traditional DLSS itself. I've been playing around with it a lot this past week, even to the point of jamming it into Football Manager 26 just to see what would happen. And, y'know what, I kinda like the result so I'm keeping it. I wasn't expecting that, and I also wasn't expecting this technology, created by Nvidia, to appear so quickly on AMD GPUs. Historically we've found that where Nvidia goes, so AMD follows, at least in the GPU feature space, but it seems like AMD might not actually have to do much this time. items.body: If you happen to pick up a copy of NBA 2K27, in your eagerness to try out the first official implementation of Nvidia's DLSS 5 AI image tech , you won't find it labelled as such in the settings menu. Instead, it appears as a simple on/off toggle under the label "DLSS Neural Rendering." And while that might seem like a small change, I think it makes a huge amount of difference in terms of public perception. Calling it DLSS 5 in the first place was, at best, confusing. Traditional DLSS, as in the upscaling/super sampling technology, is well established at this point. While some still refuse to get on board, many have become accustomed to the idea that it works well at its primary task, running your games at lower resolutions to achieve better frame rates while outputting a high-resolution image. It's not an RPG, and I'm sure as soon as Twitch streamers get their hands on it they'll be flexing on the hardest bosses without ever upgrading their gear by a single percentage point. But for us mortals, Onimusha's runtime is padded out by a pretty boring hub world full of pretty boring upgrade materials like cotton and iron that you use to very, very slowly increase your damage, health, stamina, and Oni power gauge. It's a dull system that doesn't evolve a single bit over the entire game. There are also rarer upgrade materials that you use to unlock abilities and enhancements on the skill tree. items.title: A multi-month delay for Deus Ex turned into a huge payoff for one of its best characters, says designer Harvey Smith
items.summary: Smith's story about the late stages of Deus Ex development takes some time to get to the point, but it's a fun ride.
items.body: Nobody likes game delays. Sure, a delay is temporary and suck is forever , as Gabe Newell once said, but it still chafes. But sometimes a little extra development time can go a very long way. In a new interview with the NoClip podcast , immersive sim maestro Harvey Smith shared one such story about Deus Ex, explaining how it leveraged some extra post-production time to give a much bigger role to one of the game's most famous NPCs—and make it a much better game in the process. Smith's tale actually followed a remark by Ben Horne, his co-founder at the new Black Pony Immersive studio, who said, "You can elevate a good immersive sim into a great immersive sim in a very short amount of time, a matter of months, if you just protect a post-production time." Publishers generally don't want to hear that, Smith added—although he obviously agrees with the sentiment—and so 20-some years ago, when Ion Storm Austin asked Eidos for more time to tighten up Deus Ex, "We geared up for this giant fight." items.title: The bizarre spirit of classic Elder Scrolls games is alive and well in little lo-fi RPG A Short Quest
items.summary: A few hours with a recent playtest has me eager to play the full thing next year.
items.body: When a big old tree talks, I listen. He said, "I have a task of great importance," as soon as I opened my eyes, and who was I to turn him down? "Take this note to the King, it should be a short quest," he instructed, and although there is no king in the playtest for A Short Quest , I am eager to fulfill the tree's wishes when the whole game is out next year. There are actually a lot of mysterious things I found in the few hours I spent with A Short Quest that I'd like to know more about. Every time I passed by a pond it spoke and asked me to dance (jump three times) for a blueberry. I found a note in an old mine that told me how to find the "glyph cipher" on the side of a cart, but I still don't know what to do with it. And I'm still not sure why I was summoned into the underground domain of a ghost wizard who tried to kill me. A Short Quest reminded me of when I would watch a friend from middle school play Morrowind on his Xbox or when I played Oblivion for the first time.
